purpose: Explore Earth terrain analog candidates for one fixed lunar communications-obstruction profile
selection_metric: Root mean squared difference of start-relative ground heights in meters. Lower is closer. No vertical scaling, no path stretching. Primary reference only drives ranking.
quality_method: Require SRTM-origin NUM 1–23, SWB land, valid heights, one-cell native quality erosion, and all four bilinear sampling supports passing the reprojected mask. Final native support codes checked again. NUM is source/count metadata, not a height-uncertainty estimate.
sampling: Entire Earth tile bilinearly reprojected to aligned EPSG:32613 30m cells. Both planets sampled at 75 equal-distance locations (~29.76m apart). Lunar fixed 30m mean DEM as previously documented. Original baseline re-evaluated on the same Earth grid.
physics: 2m base/rover, 5m peak-relay trial. Approximate spherical curvature, Earth R=6371000m. No atmosphere, Fresnel-zone or RF propagation model.
limitations: Geometry-only retrieval within one 1-degree tile, not a global optimum or verified new analog discovery.
Ranked matches are selected on the same data used to report fit. Nearby lunar references are secondary diagnostics, not independent validation.
Land cover, geology, human structures, accessibility, ownership and permissions remain unverified.
Water/source masks do not establish a bare-earth terrain model or an operational site.
Earth elevation uncertainty is not quantified. Lower RMSE is not a probability of mission success.
30m grid spacing does not imply 30m effective resolution or equivalent accuracy across planets.
Trial lines are antenna links, not drivable rover routes.
All marker elevations are ground heights; antenna heights are attributes.
network_method: Minimum hops on an increasing-index graph of the same 75 sample positions; endpoints 2m, relay candidates 5m. Edges require positive nominal sampled clearance including curvature. Tie-break maximizes the minimum sampled interior clearance. Not a deployment design, a 2D optimum, or uncertainty-aware.
